display.purpose: The game name in the pelmet; white fill over a 5px ink keyline painted first (4px when short).

headline.purpose: Big top-bar numerals; 24px at heights of 500px and below.

flat-title.purpose: Title in a flat's royal header; white over a 4px ink keyline painted first; 24px when short.

item-name.purpose: What is being placed, in the tray; 19px when short.

action.purpose: Primary action label (Place) in display type.

size-tag.purpose: Footprint sizes in flat rows and the tray, royal blue.

body.purpose: All running text; tabular numerals; 60ch max in cards.

button.purpose: Card button labels and the tray verdict line; verdict 14px when short.

label.purpose: Tiny uppercase tracked caps naming a column once: blush on the pelmet, royal on a flat; 10px when short.

shadows.name: paper-lift
shadows.purpose: The only UI shadow: lifts floating card pieces (stage buttons, flats, the tray, the notice) off the stage. No hard offset block shadows.

shadows.name: world-sun
shadows.value: Three.js DirectionalLight #ffffff intensity 1.35 at (-10, 20, 12) from the board centre, PCF shadow map 4096, bias -0.0006; AmbientLight #ffffff 2.1
shadows.purpose: Real soft shadows in the diorama. Day-cycle light shift (warm dusk, dim night) is planned, not built.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for all UI state transitions.

motion.name: meter-slide
motion.purpose: Loved/Feared thumb moving to a new position.

motion.name: button-press
motion.purpose: Stage and card button hover and press.

motion.name: flat-on
motion.value: 420ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); translateX(105%) to translateX(-6px) rotate(-0.4deg) at 70%, then rest
motion.purpose: A panel flat slides on from the right wing with a small paper settle.

motion.name: tray-on
motion.purpose: The placing tray slides up from the foot of the stage.

motion.name: building-drop
motion.value: 0.42s cubic ease-out (1 - p)^3; from 0.7 above the board and 0.12 rad tilt to flat
motion.purpose: A newly placed building drops onto the board. The starting town never drops.

motion.name: occluder-fade
motion.value: opacity to 0.3, exponential approach (1 - 0.001^dt); ink hidden below 0.6
motion.purpose: Walls, gatehouses and buildings blocking the placement footprint fade, and return when the view clears.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: transition: none; animation: none; building drop skipped
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion, meter and buttons snap, flats and the tray appear in place, and buildings land without dropping.

breakpoints.name: short
breakpoints.purpose: Phones held sideways: 56px pelmet, 16px scallops, tighter type ramp (display 22, headline 24, label 10, flat title 24, tray name 19, row 16 with 44px rows, verdict 14).

breakpoints.name: coarse
breakpoints.purpose: Hides the camera turn buttons (camera turning is a PC extra). The Build button stays.

outlines.name: world-ink
outlines.purpose: Diorama edges: grass rim, wooden base, wall and gatehouse boxes, building wall boxes and roof outlines, and road edges only where road meets grass.

outlines.name: row-rule
outlines.purpose: The one divider between flat rows; none above the first row.

outlines.name: disabled
outlines.purpose: Outline and text of a disabled control.

outlines.name: focus
outlines.purpose: Keyboard focus on every focusable element (flat rows draw it inside, offset -4px); the map shows a 4px marigold frame below the pelmet instead, hidden while placing.

outlines.name: placement-footprint
outlines.purpose: Outer edge of the placement footprint; leaf or curtain fill beneath at 0.72 opacity.

components.name: Pelmet
components.description: Curtain-red valance with a scalloped ink-edged hem holding the crest and big-number stats.
components.css: .ds-pelmet { position: relative; height: 76px; padding: 0 24px; margin-bottom: 25px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 36px; background: #c8324a; border-bottom: 3px solid #3b2a2e; color: #fff; } .ds-pelmet::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: -25px; height: 22px; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 0, #c8324a 17px, #3b2a2e 17px 20px, transparent 20.5px) 0 0 / 48px 22px; background-repeat: round no-repeat; } .ds-crest { font: 400 30px/1 'Lilita One', 'Nunito', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.01em; -webkit-text-stroke: 5px #3b2a2e; paint-order: stroke fill; } .ds-stats { display: flex; gap: 28px; margin: 0; } .ds-stat { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; } .ds-stat dt { font: 800 11px/1 'Nunito', sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #fff2f4; } .ds-stat dd { margin: 0; font: 400 32px/1.05 'Lilita One', sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

narrative.overview:
The kingdom is a paper stage. The papercraft diorama town is the stage floor and owns the whole window; the interface is theatre trim around its edges. M0 built the first of that trim: a curtain-red pelmet with a scalloped hem across the top, carrying the kingdom's name and its numbers, and round printed-card buttons resting on the stage. M1 added the first panel flat (the Build list, sliding on from the right wing in its wooden groove) and the placing tray at the foot of the stage. Everything, chrome and world alike, reads as printed card stock: flat hand-coloured fills, one dark ink outline, and soft paper shadows.

The feel is bright, warm and readable: a storybook kingdom made of simple shapes. Density is low; the town comes first and the chrome second. Big numerals over tiny capital labels let the player read their day at a glance. The world refuses the category default of parchment scrolls in carved wood frames; the wood here is a toy stage's base, floorboards and the grooves the flats run in, not ornament.

The diorama sits on an ink-edged wooden board (base wood) standing on a plank stage floor, lit by a white sun with real soft shadows over a pale sky. Inside stone walls with gatehouses lie a flagstone plaza, cobble and dirt roads, a statue and a quest board as camera-facing cut-outs, and papercraft buildings folded from drawn panels. Grass carries fixed-seed tufts, so the board looks the same on every load; the square grid appears only while building.
keyCharacteristics: One ink colour outlines everything, in the UI and in the 3D world.
Flat fills only; colour changes are hard edges, never blends.
Marigold means "what you are doing right now" and nothing else.
Display numerals in a heavy rounded playbill face; body in a rounded workhorse.
Theatre trim stays on the edges of the stage; the map is never boxed in.
Keyboard first, with a visible marigold focus on everything focusable.

rules.name: The Right Now Rule
rules.body: Marigold (#f2b233) marks only what the player is doing right now: keyboard focus, the placement footprint, the chosen route. If an element is marigold while idle, it is wrong. When two right-now signals would compete, one steps aside: while placing, the map's focus frame hides and the footprint outline carries the focus.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Ink (#3b2a2e) is the only outline colour, for the UI and the world. No grey borders, no coloured strokes, no second ink. The two ink tints are part of the same ink, not new colours: the row rule divides rows inside a flat, and faint ink outlines a disabled control.

rules.name: The Flat Fill Rule
rules.body: Fills are flat. Where CSS gradients appear (the meter halves, the scallops) they are hard stops used to draw shapes, never blends. No soft colour gradients anywhere.

rules.name: The Big Number, Tiny Label Rule
rules.body: Readouts are large display type over a tiny uppercase label. The label names the column once; it is never repeated per row.

rules.name: The Stage Owns the Screen Rule
rules.body: Chrome lives on the edges; the town is never boxed in or covered by a frame.

rules.name: The Soft Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft and ink-tinted only. No hard offset block shadows.

dos: Do outline every UI piece and world edge in ink (#3b2a2e): 3px in the UI, 3.5px in the world.
Do keep marigold (#f2b233) for what the player is doing right now: focus, placement footprint, chosen route.
Do give every focusable element a visible 4px marigold focus outline.
Do set stat labels in blush (#fff2f4) on curtain red (#c8324a), as tiny tracked caps over big numerals.
Do use the single paper-lift shadow (0 3px 10px rgb(59 42 46 / 0.22)) for floating card pieces.
Do use the shared 52px round stage button for anything resting on the stage.
Do put a flat's primary action in leaf button with ink text, and write success and problem text in deep leaf and deep curtain.
Do keep a verdict on its own row so the buttons never move.
Do check every layout at 844x390 landscape.
Do keep camera turning a PC extra, hidden on coarse pointers.
Do keep theatre trim on the edges of the stage and in story moments.
donts: Don't use marigold as decoration, brand accent or idle fill.
Don't introduce a second outline colour or grey borders.
Don't blend gradients; colour changes are hard edges.
Don't use hard offset block shadows.
Don't put theatre trim inside lists.
Don't print key hints on screen; keys come from the bindings table.
Don't paint the build grid into the grass; it shows only while building.
Don't reach for parchment scrolls or carved wood frames.
